key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: Why is a small deed not considered insignificant in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) taught that a deed is not considered small or insignificant if it is performed with taqwa (God-consciousness/piety). Since God accepts such deeds, they cannot be belittled. This hadith, found in al-Kafi, underscores the Shia emphasis on the qualitative value of actions rooted in divine awareness, linking the Prophet's legacy to the Imams' teachings on spiritual merit.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Fuzayl Bin Usman, from Abu Ubeyda, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Do not belittle a deed performed with piety, and how can one belittle what is Accepted?’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Fudayl ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Ubaydah from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Amir al-Mu’minin (Ali ibn abu Talib) (a.s.) would say, ‘A deed with piety is never considered a little deed. How could it be considered little when it is the very thing with which deeds are accepted?”’
